author: agileacademyinsights
desc: Elon Musk is basically telling his competitors: Go ahead. Copy our rockets. In this interview, Musk says SpaceX doesn't use patents to stop competitors from copying its technology. There's even a rocket outside the company's headquarters that anyone can inspect. Whether copying a rocket is quite that simple is another question. But the leadership question goes beyond protecting a design. Competitors can study a product, understand the technology and hire experienced engineers. Reproducing the way an organization keeps improving is much harder. How do people solve problems together? How quickly can they make decisions? Can teams experiment, learn from failures and apply what they discover? At Agile Academy, we believe those capabilities deserve as much attention as the products they help create. Protecting what a company has already built is only part of the work. Leaders also need to make sure their teams can build what comes next. Catching up with a product is one thing. author: jaxdecon
desc: Trigger warning: blood and biohazard cleanup footage. Where do you start when an accident leaves a hotel room covered in biohazard contamination? Thankfully, this person survived and emergency services were able to help. While they’re recovering, I’m stepping into the room for the next six, seven, maybe eight hours to work through the cleanup. This is another side of crime scene cleanup: responding to accidents and medical emergencies that leave behind blood and contaminated materials. Hotel biohazard cleanup doesn’t always involve a crime, but it still requires careful work. The first step on this job is identifying the main source of contamination. Here, that’s the bed. The room might look overwhelming, but having a starting point turns that scene into a process. We begin with bulk removal: removing contaminated bedding and other affected materials, packing the waste into red biohazard bags and boxes, and working through what needs to come out. This is the part of blood cleanup that happens before we can address the surfaces and contamination underneath. Bagging everything up isn’t the end of the job, either. The biohazard waste from this cleanup goes to a dedicated facility for proper disposal. I’m sharing the work behind hotel accident cleanup—from that first walkthrough to removing the biggest source of biohazard. Every room has a different situation, and behind every cleanup is a person whose life was interrupted. Follow Jax Decon for a firsthand look at crime scene cleanup, blood cleanup, and biohazard remediation in Jacksonville, Florida. What would you tackle first walking into this room? #BiohazardCleanup #CrimeSceneCleanup #904

desc: The $30,000 computer that runs Wall Street 🖥️ The Bloomberg Terminal is the most important machine in finance. It has black screens, orange text and a keyboard with yellow, red and a green "GO" key, and it costs around $30,000 a year per user. More than 300,000 traders, bankers and fund managers pay for it to see every stock, bond and currency in real time, and to chat with each other on its built-in messaging system. It was created by Michael Bloomberg after Salomon Brothers pushed him out in 1981 with about $10 million from his partnership stake. His first customer was Merrill Lynch. Today the terminal brings in more than 85% of Bloomberg L.P.'s revenue and made him one of the richest people in the world. desc: Max Did Not Expect Ray To Become A Diva! 💅😭 #clips #tiktok #fyp #fypシ #fypシ゚viral #viral_video #viralnow #trending #usa #funny #meme #plaqueboymax #rayasianboy  During a school exchange trip to Japan in July 2023, Ray learned that Kai was broadcasting nearby and followed clues from the livestream to a 7-Eleven, where he approached him. Their encounter was captured on the stream and circulated online. Kai later visited Taiwan for Ray's high-school graduation in 2024 and invited him to the United States. Ray subsequently created content with Kai and other members of AMP. At the 2024 Streamer Awards, Ray was nominated for Best Breakout Streamer. In March 2025, Ray appeared in the GQ Sports video series 10 Essentials. The Central News Agency reported that the video reached number five on YouTube's United States trending list within seven hours of publication. In June 2025, Ray played in a creator charity basketball game in Houston. He made four three-point shots during the game, including one from near midcourt. In October 2025, GQ Taiwan published what it described as Ray's first exclusive magazine interview. In the interview, Ray said that his time with Kai and other AMP members had shown him how successful creators handled their careers and had helped him remain grounded.

author: quanillionaire
desc: This hilarious moment features former UFC champion Quinton Jackson when he misunderstands the phrase "gated community" and initially interprets it as "gay community." In the clip, he sees the sign and pauses with a genuinely puzzled expression, clearly trying to process what he thinks he just read. Instead of recognizing it as a normal real-estate term describing a secured residential area with controlled access, he assumes it is referring to a type of community of people, which completely shifts the meaning in his mind. The humor comes from that immediate mismatch between his interpretation and the actual meaning. While the audience instantly understands "gated community," he treats it like unfamiliar or oddly labeled social terminology, which makes his reaction feel both serious and unintentionally funny. His facial expression and tone add to the effect because he isn't joking-he's genuinely trying to make sense of it in real time, which amplifies the confusion. #fypシ #fypシ゚viral #quanillionaire
stickers: The level of misunderstanding is outmatched  😂

author: realraywilliam
desc: Bunch of weirdass people 😑 - - The Laverne Pavlinac story is a bizarre case of a false confession that derailed a murder investigation and allowed a serial killer to remain free. In 1990, following the murder of 23-year-old Taunja Bennett in Portland, Oregon, 57-year-old Pavlinac concocted a detailed lie to frame her abusive boyfriend, John Sosnovske, as a desperate way to get him out of her life. She eventually implicated herself as an accomplice, leading to both of them being convicted and sentenced to life in prison in 1991, despite Pavlinac recanting her story at trial. Because police closed the case based on her fabrications, the real perpetrator—the notorious "Happy Face Killer" Keith Hunter Jesperson- went undetected and murdered at least seven more women over the next several years.

author: bycoastra
desc: Kevin Garnett played basketball with an intensity that was impossible to ignore. From entering the NBA straight out of high school in 1995 to becoming an MVP in Minnesota and an NBA champion in Boston, Garnett gave everything he had to the game. The emotion, the passion, and the competitiveness became part of his identity. But behind that intensity was a person who didn’t always feel comfortable letting others see what he was feeling. There’s something interesting about that contrast. Sometimes the people who appear the toughest are the ones who have learned to keep the most to themselves. And maybe strength isn’t always about how well you hide what you’re feeling. Sometimes it’s being comfortable enough to let people see it. ⚓️ - ➸ Curious how these edits come together? author: eliteathletesdevelopment
desc: Football performance isn't just about how quickly you move. It's also about how quickly you recognise what is happening around you. Before kick-off, RC Strasbourg's Martial Godo incorporates visual activation into his warm-up, preparing his eyes and brain for the perceptual demands of competition. Football is an environment of constant information processing. Every movement requires players to detect relevant cues, interpret what they mean and organise an appropriate response, often within fractions of a second. For an attacking player like Godo, this might involve recognising a defender's body orientation, identifying space to accelerate into, anticipating an opponent's movement or adjusting his actions based on the position of teammates. This is where the relationship between perception and action becomes so important. Visual activation exercises aim to prepare aspects of visual attention, tracking and responsiveness before entering the unpredictable environment of a match. However, effective visual performance isn't simply about seeing more or reacting faster to an isolated stimulus. It's about identifying the right information at the right time and using it to guide football-specific decisions. That's an important distinction. While isolated visual exercises can form part of a pre-match routine, their direct transfer to match performance isn't guaranteed. Scanning, anticipation and decision-making must also be developed through representative football situations where perception and movement are closely connected. Physical preparation gets the body ready to perform. Perceptual preparation considers the information that guides those movements. Because being physically ready means very little if you're consistently late to recognise what's happening around you.
stickers:
MARTIAL GODO’S UNIQUE
WARM-UP ROUTINE👀 preparing his brain to recognise visual cues and respond to the rapidly changing demands of football.

desc: GTA 6 road rage is more realistic than my city 🚗 YourRAGE #yourrage #gta6 #fyp #viral GTA 6 is finally here. After two delays and more than a decade of waiting since GTA 5, Grand Theft Auto VI dropped on November 19, 2026 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, and it's already on track to be the biggest launch in gaming history. GTA 5 set the record back in 2013 with 11.2 million copies sold in 24 hours, and analysts expect GTA 6 to sell somewhere between 37 and 51 million copies in its first week. This time Rockstar took the series back to Vice City, but it's only one part of the map. The whole game is set in Leonida, their version of Florida, with the Leonida Keys, the Grassrivers swamps, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia and the Mount Kalaga wilderness up north. You play as Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, two criminals whose heist goes wrong and pulls them into a conspiracy that spreads across the whole state. Everyone's streaming it right now and the reactions have been insane. Which part of the map are you going to first, and is GTA 6 living up to the hype for you?
